frontier.hypothesis: j4read - the exact target frame at only +25 body lines - can be made byte-neutral by placing its two extra indexed-Judge sites where jump2 cross-jumping removes their emitted code
frontier.mechanism: s4 measured a statement duplicated into all four arms of the kind chain being re-merged by jump2 at NEGATIVE cost (armjoin1: 139 insns vs the base's 140). The s3/s4 attempts placed extra sites in line, where nothing can remove them; the surplus is now itemised as exactly two lh/addu/andi/sll/lh/addu triples, so the question is whether a duplicated placement exists whose merged tail coincides with insns the target already emits.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate placements for the 3rd and 4th sites that put IDENTICAL Judge-reading tails in two or more blocks that jump2 can cross-jump: the four kind-chain arms (payload must be a statement the join already contains), the /32 bgez join spelled as an explicit if/else, and the loop-break vs loop-exit paths. Measure each with INSTR=1 frame5.py, accepting only vars=24 with bodydiff trending toward 0, and read tmp/grind/func_80030580/dumps/code6cac_b.jump2 to confirm whether the merge fired.

frontier.hypothesis: A fourth generator exists that fires on a construct func_80030580 already contains, supplying the missing two slots without adding a Judge site
frontier.mechanism: Three generators are now known: the indexed-global fold (sites-1), the truncated magic-multiply division (sites), and the HImode-bitwise phantom form (inert here). Each was found by reducing a corpus witness to a minimal standalone repro, and s5/genprobe.py now makes that reduction cost one cc1 run. Only a generator firing on a pointer-biv loop, a struct copy, a 32x32 multiply with >>12, a shift-based signed divide or a four-arm equality chain can close this function.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run tmp/grind/func_80030580/s3/census3.py to list every leaf with vars>0, drop the witnesses whose C contains an indexed global or a truncated constant division (both now explained), and reduce each remaining witness to a minimal standalone repro in the s5/gen2.c style, bisecting it with genprobe.py until the firing sub-expression is isolated. Then test the isolated shape in-function with frame5.py.

frontier.hypothesis: The target's vars=24 is not three 8-byte orphans; MIPS_STACK_ALIGN only pins it to 17..24, so 8+8+4 or 8+16 also round to 24
frontier.mechanism: Every session since s2 has assumed three orphans because a corpus census of OUR compiled C never produced a non-spill_new leaf slot - an argument about the sample, not about the target. s1 only ever tested one non-spill_new shape (a Vec3i tmp local, which does touch sp), so the space of constructs that allocate an untouched stack_temp / stack_local in a leaf is essentially unexplored.
frontier.next_probe: Use s5/genprobe.py to enumerate constructs that produce a non-spill_new ctx= with ZERO ($sp) accesses in a leaf: unions, casts between struct types, a struct-typed conditional expression, a struct-valued comma expression, a struct copy whose destination is immediately overwritten, and a 4-byte object alongside the existing orphan. Any hit that emits no sp traffic is then spelled in-function and measured for bodydiff with frame5.py.
